quote:
Terracing 
is useful in situations where runoff is common but cannot 
be adequately controlled by other soil conservation practices 
and where the intensity and volume of runoff surpass the 
water storage capacity of the soil. Terraces are generally 
recommended for slopes of 4–50 percent (Rufino, 1989). 
Short slopes with a gradient of less than 4 percent should be 
protected by contour vegetation barriers, contour planting or 
strip cropping. On longer slopes, the land should be terraced 
if the slope gradient is greater than 0.5 percent (FAO, 2000a) 
(case study 26).

relationship.gate: The source recommends terraces by slope and slope length when runoff cannot be adequately controlled by other soil conservation practices and exceeds soil water storage capacity.
relationship.note: Conditional terrace selection guidance. General recommended range and long-slope alternative are preserved in reported_values; no independent lower/upper exclusion, optimum response, monotonic direction or suitability score is established.

context.practice_as_described: Terraces on sloping land to hold water and soil and reduce runoff velocity for trees and crops. Alternatives are simpler soil conservation practices; on short gentle slopes the source recommends contour vegetation barriers, contour planting or strip cropping.
context.note: Box 4.4 Collecting and conserving water starts PDF79 and continues through PDF81. Terrace bullet begins PDF79 and continues PDF80; this slope guidance applies to slope-reshaping terraces, not a default for every microcatchment technology listed in the box. No named terrace subtype is established. This is source guidance, not an applied spatial model, experiment, or global eligibility rule. The current source was registered for forest restoration; this staged record requires explicit water-harvesting canonical-source reuse. Existing forest evidence remains unchanged.

reported_values.short_slope_alternative: less than 4 percent: contour vegetation barriers, contour planting or strip cropping
reported_values.length_definition: short and longer are not numerically defined
reported_values.status: Source values retained; conditional selection guidance, not calibrated eligibility limits.

model_use.method: Conditional technique selection guidance in a synthesis box; no source weights or scored spatial model.

context.calibration_hold: No numerical slope-length definition, terrace-type-specific calibration, scores, endpoint closure or ecological exclusion claims. The long-slope recommendation prevents interpreting 4 percent as an absolute minimum. Do not impose 50 percent as an exclusion or invent an optimum range.
context.remaining_decision: Human review of source-specific slope/length guidance and future transfer; no automatic synthesis approval.

lineage_of: Rufino, R.L. (1989). Terraceamento. In Manual Técnico do Subprograma de Manejo e Conservação do Solo, Curitiba. Secretaria da Agricultura e do Abastecimento, Paraná, pp. 218–235; FAO (2000a), as cited by FAO Forestry Paper 175.
attribution: FAO Forestry Paper 175 (2015), Box 4.4 continuation, printed p58 / PDF80, cites Rufino (1989) for general terrace slope recommendation and FAO (2000a) for the long-slope exception. Neither cited primary source independently read in this pass.
